subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
label: JobSeeker Payment maximum rate, single with no children (per fortnight)
context: The most a single person with no children can get before tax. Income and assets can reduce it. The rates are updated on 20 March and 20 September.

subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
label: JobSeeker Payment maximum rate, single with dependent children (per fortnight)
context: The most a single person with a dependent child or children can get before tax. It is also the rate for a single person aged 55 or older after 9 continuous months on an income support payment, and for a single person assessed as having a partial capacity to work of less than 15 hours a week.

subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
label: JobSeeker Payment maximum rate, partnered (per fortnight)
context: The most a partnered person can get before tax. Income and assets, including a partner's income, can reduce it.

subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
label: JobSeeker Payment maximum rate, single principal carer with an exemption (per fortnight)
context: The most a single principal carer can get before tax when granted an exemption from mutual obligation requirements for foster caring, non-parent relative caring under a court order, home schooling, distance education or a large family.

subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
label: JobSeeker Payment minimum age
context: The youngest age at which a person can get JobSeeker Payment. The upper limit is Age Pension age.

subcategory_description: Payments from the government for people who are out of work or on leave.
context: JobSeeker Payment is available from the minimum age up to Age Pension age.

subject_meta_description: JobSeeker Payment maximum rates in Australia: {fact:au_jobseeker_single} for a single person with no children and {fact:au_jobseeker_partnered} for a partnered person, every fortnight.
